s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulcerative lesion with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological findings of dense diffuse infiltrate with lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Medical history of well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years
No systemic complaints
No history of high-risk behavior for HIV
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Histopathological examination showed dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells
Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halo found on histopathological examination
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halo found on histopathological examination, consistent with histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of yeast forms on histopathological examination, similar to blastomycosis

shortlist.label: Paracoccidioidomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic oral ulcerative lesion with granulomatous inflammation, similar to paracoccidioidomycosis

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of yeast forms on histopathological examination, although less common in oral lesions

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation on histopathological examination, although less likely given the presence of yeast forms

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo on histopathological examination, along with a dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells, is consistent with histoplasmosis, especially in the context of a nonhealing oral ulcer.

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: While blastomycosis can cause similar symptoms, the specific finding of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo is more characteristic of histoplasmosis.

rejected.label: Paracoccidioidomycosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more systemic symptoms and a different geographic distribution.

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: The lack of central nervous system involvement and the specific histopathological findings make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The presence of intracellular yeasts is not consistent with sarcoidosis, which typically presents with non-caseating granulomas without fungal elements.
